title: Unvalidated client_id length in CONNECT leads to stack buffer overflow
label: TP
evidence: src/mqtt.c:239-241 attacker-controlled cid_len copied into client_id[64] with NUL at [cid_len]
src/mqtt.h:40 MQTT_CLIENT_ID_LEN is 64
src/mqtt.h:181 client_id[MQTT_CLIENT_ID_LEN]
src/server.c:858-865 io_event io and its packet are stack locals in process_message
reason: 16-bit client ID length from CONNECT is copied into a 64-byte field on the process_message stack with no bound check; pre-auth stack overflow.

title: Unsigned integer underflow in PUBLISH remaining-length parsing causes huge allocation and exit()
label: TP
evidence: src/mqtt.c:314 len -= (sizeof(u16) + topiclen) on unsigned usize without validation
src/mqtt.c:315-316 len becomes payloadlen and is passed to unpack_bytes
src/pack.c:411-417 unpack_bytes does try_alloc(len + 1) then memcpy(dest, buf, len)
src/memory.c:49-52 try_alloc exits the process when allocation fails
reason: A topic length larger than the remaining length wraps usize; the huge size reaches unpack_bytes, causing a failing allocation and exit() (remote DoS).

title: Integer underflow in SUBSCRIBE/UNSUBSCRIBE parsing leads to endless loop and OOB reads
label: TP
evidence: src/mqtt.c:342-358 subscribe loop subtracts u16 lengths from usize len
src/mqtt.c:355 len -= topic_len with no check that topic_len fits
src/mqtt.c:386-401 unsubscribe loop uses the same pattern
reason: Oversized topic length underflows the loop counter, making the tuple loop non-terminating while reallocating and reading past the packet.

title: NULL/out-of-bounds function-pointer dispatch for packet types 2, 9 and 11
